title: Professional native-first synthesis and DSP
scope: Synthesizer sound generation, DSP fidelity, quality qualification and cross-host rendering; complements docs/song-rollout.md instead of replacing its Song-specific stages.
mission: Deliver professionally viable editable instruments that sound correct in native desktop/mobile production and natively in pre-programmed, while retaining a compatible web studio wherever technically feasible.

platform_policy.web: maintain_when_feasible; never constrain native audio quality to Web Audio or web packaging limits
platform_policy.professional_quality_gate: native reference implementations must pass acoustic and CPU benchmarks even if web support requires an explicit degraded mode
platform_policy.portability: portable patch/automation/event semantics with host-specific DSP implementations verified by reference fixtures
platform_policy.real_time: avoid allocation, blocking I/O, locks and GC-sensitive work in audio callback
platform_policy.backwards_compatibility: version schema when interpretation changes; maintain documented migrations and legacy reads
platform_policy.data_storage: store audio bytes as external assets; keep .premidi files declarative and inspectable

architectural_decisions.decision: Separate platform-neutral synth graph and parameter/event semantics from the current Web Audio voice implementation.
Prototype suitable portable DSP engines/frameworks for native desktop/mobile before committing to C++, Rust, JUCE, WebAssembly or another specific toolchain.
Use shared test fixtures and reference audio analysis to establish host parity; bit-identical floating-point samples are not assumed across implementations.
Introduce a new versioned synth patch schema only when its meaning changes; do not break existing v7 Beat/v8 Song imports.
Web compatibility is best effort without silent sound substitutions; capabilities and unsupported features must be detectable.

must_pass: browser regression checks on compatible PRs
verification_policy.thresholds: document test inputs, reference hardware and tolerances before claiming an objective performance metric
non_goals: claim state-of-the-art quality on feature count alone
silently replace native sounds with samples
sacrifice native DSP to preserve browser support

phases.title: Native applications, game integration and qualification

tasks.title: Correct note-off and envelope state
acceptance: An early release begins from the actual attack/decay level, with no jump to sustain.
Long notes retain intended ADSR durations.
Synth preview and offline rendering use the same envelope contract.

tasks.title: Oversampled nonlinear drive
acceptance: Distortion on synth and sampler uses 4x oversampled WaveShaper where supported.
Spectrum benchmarks quantify aliasing at representative pitches and drive settings.
Native DSP backend reproduces equivalent anti-aliasing behavior.

tasks.title: Measured audio quality regression harness
acceptance: Automated tests measure alias-to-signal energy, DC offset, peaks, attack/release discontinuities and RMS.
Reference renders and threshold metadata are versioned; regressions fail CI.
Test results distinguish browser/device variance from DSP defects.

tasks.title: Polyphony and shared voice lifecycle
acceptance: Voice budget and stealing policy are explicit and deterministic.
32 sustained voices are glitch-free on a specified desktop reference configuration.
Stop/seek/loop cannot leak oscillators or drop shared delay tails.

tasks.title: Master headroom, monitoring and export fidelity
acceptance: Peak/RMS and true-peak measurement report clipping rather than concealing it.
16-/24-bit PCM and 32-bit float output paths are specified, with dithering where appropriate.
Export sample-rate conversion meets a measured fidelity target.

tasks.title: Host-neutral synth graph and versioned DSP contracts
acceptance: Patch interpretation requires no DOM, microphone, IndexedDB or window object.
Parameter identifiers and units are stable and versioned, with explicit migration.
The same canonical events and patch semantics feed standalone, game and optional web renderers.

tasks.title: Real-time native DSP host design
acceptance: Choose and document a maintained native DSP toolchain and mobile/desktop audio-device adapters based on prototypes.
Audio callback performs no unbounded allocation, I/O, locks or UI work.
Device sample-rate, buffer-size, underrun and suspend/resume behavior is tested.

tasks.title: Web host compatibility adapter
acceptance: Web support may fall back only through declared and user-visible compatibility modes.
Web limitations cannot reduce native synthesis capability or corrupt native patches.
Unsupported capabilities do not silently render as a different instrument.

tasks.title: General modulation matrix
acceptance: Velocity, key tracking, envelopes and LFOs can target multiple supported synthesis parameters.
Bipolar/unipolar ranges, depth, polarity and modulation rate are explicit.
Modulation is deterministic under offline rendering and gameplay control.

tasks.title: Sample-accurate automation and smoothing
acceptance: Parameter changes during sustained notes are smooth and free of zipper noise.
Beat definition, Song override and game state commands have an explicit precedence contract.
Recorded movements survive native project round-trip.

tasks.title: Morphing wavetable and phase modulation
acceptance: Interpolation is continuous; band-limiting avoids obvious aliasing.
Frequency/phase modulation is available with independently routable depths.
Original harmonic patches retain sound identity via migrations.

tasks.title: Expanded filters and routing
acceptance: Multiple filter stages may run serially or in parallel.
Ladder, comb and formant options are benchmarked for resonance and stability.
Extreme modulation does not generate NaNs, runaway gain or unstable feedback.

tasks.title: Granular, spectral and transient models
acceptance: Grain scheduling and time-varying partials are project-portable.
Attacks, sustained harmonics and noise can evolve independently.
Native playback does not require retaining entire long recordings in memory.

tasks.title: Production-ready multisampling and time stretch
acceptance: Sustain loops and crossfades are supported.
Independent pitch and time adjustment has measurable quality limits.
External asset paths remain portable, verified and separate from .premidi JSON.

tasks.title: Routable professional effects
acceptance: Chorus, reverb, EQ, compressors and upgraded delay have predictable tails.
Per-voice and shared-bus effects are distinct to bound CPU cost.
Effect routing is versioned, bypassable, automatable and recallable.

tasks.title: MIDI, MPE and expressive performance
acceptance: Velocity can shape timbre, not only gain.
MIDI note input, sustain and pitch-bend behavior are verified.
Where supported, independent per-note expression is preserved in native files.

tasks.title: Objective synth conversion and comparison
acceptance: Fit time-varying harmonics and transients, not only averaged spectra.
Report perceptual/audio error and disclose irreducible mismatch.
Test several pitch ranges, velocities, attacks and noisy sources.

tasks.title: Native desktop reference application
acceptance: Standalone desktop works without browser/network runtime.
Offline render and device playback match canonical DSP fixtures.
Can save and reopen .premidi plus external audio assets.

tasks.title: Native mobile host and lifecycle
acceptance: Suspend/resume and device-rate changes preserve voice state or terminate safely.
Audio remains responsive under representative mobile CPU and thermal constraints.
Touch editing uses same native project semantics.

tasks.title: pre-programmed playback and control parity
acceptance: The game engine loads versioned native patch and Song definitions.
Game state modulates documented parameters without a second music script language.
Matched reference renders prove interpretation parity and preserve legacy files.

tasks.title: Professional release qualification
acceptance: Document low-latency performance on reference desktop and mobile devices.
Prove project round-trip, crash recovery, stable rendering and tested polyphony.
Publish measured limitations and regressions without claiming fidelity from mere feature existence.
